$comment: The contexts a skill's `bound-to` draws from, one entry per context with its parent, its kind, what it means, and the noun a role phrase names it by; the rules for reading and extending this file are in skills/skill-authoring/SKILL.md.

universal.means: Any reader, whatever their language, version control system, hosting platform or agent tool.

language.means: A reader writing in some programming language.

node.means: A reader writing JavaScript on Node.js.

vcs.means: A reader with a version control system.

git.means: A reader whose version control system is git.

platform.means: A reader with a hosted service the work is carried out on.

forge.means: A reader whose platform offers proposed changes for review, whatever it calls them.

github.means: A reader whose forge is GitHub.

gitlab.means: A reader whose forge is GitLab.

tracker.means: A reader with an issue tracker, whether or not the forge hosts it.

agent-tool.means: A reader working as an agent through tools of its own.

claude-code.means: A reader whose agent tool is Claude Code.
